findings.evidence: The public term symbol denotes discovery evidence, exact query text, selector-or-query positional input, graph lookup input, and mutation target input across symbol, relation, graph, and change routes.
findings.requiredResolution: Reserve query for untrusted discovery or resolution text, symbol for resolved records, selector for exact symbol identity, and node-selector for graph identity.
findings.resolutionProof: The public operation registry and inventory now reserve query, symbol, selector, node-selector, location, scope, projection, continuation, plan ID, recovery ID, and status for their canonical meanings; the inventory test rejects retired selector and paging aliases.

findings.evidence: The exact selector semantic type is exposed as selectorHandle in legacy typed operations but as positional symbol in the public adapter; continuations are exposed as page, continuation, continuationToken, and continuation.
findings.requiredResolution: Expose each semantic type under one canonical term and mechanically reject aliases in all current public projections.
findings.resolutionProof: All current public routes use --selector, --node-selector, and --continuation; registry-derived help, schemas, documentation, skill, completion, examples, and golden fixtures share those terms.

findings.evidence: External failure IDs, plan IDs, recovery IDs, and several public exact-target positions enter as String; AgentSelectorHandle and relationship tokens prove only prefixes and size locally.
findings.requiredResolution: Parse every Kast-issued primitive once into an opaque operation-, root-, generation-, or persisted-state-bound domain value before semantic execution.
findings.resolutionProof: Public boundaries refine selector, graph-node selector, continuation, plan, recovery, and external-failure primitives into typed values before semantic dispatch, with closed malformed, stale, wrong-root, and wrong-operation failures.

findings.evidence: Discovery candidates do not all carry selectorHandle, while graph nodes emit numeric IDs and graph neighbors accepts a symbol string instead of a distinct graph node selector.
findings.requiredResolution: Give every selectable search result a SymbolSelector and every selectable graph node a distinct GraphNodeSelector accepted verbatim by compatible consumers.
findings.resolutionProof: Every selectable search or resolve result carries an IssuedSymbolSelector consumed verbatim by all exact symbol operations, and graph.nodes issues an IssuedGraphNodeSelector consumed verbatim by graph.neighbors.

findings.evidence: Relationship, graph impact, rename, and replacement public paths accept qualified-name-like text and internally re-run exact resolution; explicit legacy selectors can also be reconstructed from qualified name, file, offset, kind, and container.
findings.requiredResolution: Require SymbolSelector at every exact public operation and remove qualified-name, location, offset, kind, and container reconstruction paths.
findings.resolutionProof: The closed PublicOperation variants require UntrustedSymbolSelector at exact boundaries and authenticate it to SymbolSelector; exact routes no longer accept query, qualified-name, path, offset, location, kind, or container substitutes.

findings.evidence: AgentSelectorHandle, AgentRelationPageToken, and AgentImpactPageToken constructors accept prefix-shaped strings without proving root, generation, operation, or semantic subject binding.
findings.requiredResolution: Rename boundary syntax values or strengthen construction so every domain type establishes the guarantee its name claims, with closed stale and wrong-root rejection.
findings.resolutionProof: Boundary syntax is represented as UntrustedSymbolSelector or UntrustedGraphNodeSelector until backend/root/generation authentication yields SymbolSelector or GraphNodeSelector; operation-bound continuations are authenticated by their owning operation.

findings.evidence: cli-rs/src/agent/adapter/graph.rs::resolve_selector uses symbol.starts_with("ksh1.") to decide whether one positional string is a query or selector.
findings.requiredResolution: Use distinct typed CLI fields and operation request variants; no public dispatch may inspect token contents to choose a semantic input type.
findings.resolutionProof: Clap routes and PublicOperation variants select query versus selector semantics structurally; public dispatch contains no starts_with selector inference or query fallback.

findings.evidence: Public routes live in agent_surface.rs, adapter mappings are handwritten, the private AgentCommand tree and protocol/source/commands.json define parallel operations, capabilities list only a legacy route, and skill/docs/examples contain independent command text.
findings.requiredResolution: Make one closed typed operation registry authoritative and generate or mechanically validate every public route, schema, mapping, capability, reference, skill, example, runbook, completion, and golden fixture against it.
findings.resolutionProof: OperationId and OperationDefinition generate the operation catalog, request and result schemas, RPC bindings, capabilities, CLI reference, installed skill, runbook, completion, examples, golden workflow, and benchmark fixture; integration tests run generation in --check mode and compare this inventory to the registry.
